key_insight: The paper maps medical LLM capabilities to real clinical reasoning needs using a dual clinical-computational framework, then benchmarks 18 models across five reasoning levels.
clinical_relevance: It helps identify which models are better suited for diagnosis-oriented work versus decision support and patient dialogue in healthcare workflows.
method: Built a five-level clinical competency scheme based on Miller’s Pyramid, from recall to dynamic case management.
Linked deductive, inductive, and abductive reasoning patterns to common medical tasks and goals.
Created a benchmark dataset covering five medical reasoning levels and evaluated 18 state-of-the-art models.
evidence_signal: The benchmark results show specialist medical models perform best on diagnosis-centric tasks, while general models lead in decision support and dialogue.
watch_item: The authors highlight unresolved issues such as limited data, hallucinations, and weak grounding, which can affect safe real-world deployment.
paper_title: Aligning Clinical Needs and AI Capabilities: A Survey on LLMs for Medical Reasoning
